# S8 — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping`: live Jira probe to pre-populate mapping config

## Context / Problem
Epic 3d7a (S1–S5) adds the mapping seam: a reserved `[mapping]` / `[tool.rebar.mapping]`
block with per-layer vocabulary (`statuses`, `issue_types`, `link_types`, `hierarchy`)
and axis maps (`status_map`, `type_map`, `link_map`, `priority_map`, `create_defaults`),
parsed by `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py` (S1). Hand-authoring it
is transcription-error-prone. S8 adds a READ-ONLY command that observes a live Jira
project via the pycontribs client and emits a suggested `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block
seeded with the project's real vocabulary and identity-seed axis maps.

Findings resolved:
- Verb `rebar bridge probe` COLLIDES with the retired alias `bridge-probe`
  (`_registry.py:579`; parser `_parsers/advanced/bridge.py:117`; handler `_bridge_probe`
  `_cli/__init__.py:103`, which CREATES+DELETES a throwaway issue — not read-only). New
  verb: **`rebar bridge suggest-mapping`** (verified free in `src/`+`tests/`).
- No private `_get_json` — it exists ONLY on the Gerrit client
  (`review_bot/gerrit_client.py:128`), not the jira adapter, which uses only HIGH-LEVEL
  `jira.JIRA` methods; the probe uses only such methods (below).
- No tomlkit; TOML read via stdlib `tomllib`; `_emit_toml` is fail-closed on nesting, so
  an orchestrator + dedicated nested emitter are added (below).

## Approach
New verb wired into the bridge group (NEW):
- Parser: `commands.add_parser("suggest-mapping", ...)` in
  `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/bridge.py` (beside `check-access` ~line 117), taking
  `<PROJECT>` and `--write`.
- Dispatch: add `"suggest-mapping"` to `bridge_cli`'s pass-through set
  (`src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:259`) + a `_passthrough`/`_passthrough_help`
  branch → NEW handler `_bridge_suggest_mapping` (`_cli/__init__.py`, sibling of
  `_bridge_probe`).

Probe (NEW `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_probe.py`, <800 LOC): a probe
PORT with one narrow method per axis, each a thin call to a pycontribs `jira.JIRA`
method. Default port built from `build_client_from_settings`
(`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:155`); tests inject a FAKE port → offline. Pin
`jira>=3.8,<4` (pyproject.toml:202).

Axis grounding — every axis uses a HIGH-LEVEL method (no private REST):
- `issue_types` + `hierarchy` → `jira.JIRA.issue_types()` (read each `hierarchyLevel`;
  if absent, `hierarchy` is DROPPED empty + note, not fabricated).
- `priority_map` vocab → `jira.JIRA.priorities()`; `link_types` →
  `jira.JIRA.issue_link_types()` (documented public).
- `statuses` vocab → `jira.JIRA.statuses()` (documented public). pycontribs exposes no
  per-PROJECT status list publicly, so this is the GLOBAL set — the block documents that
  honest limitation.
- `create_defaults` stubs → `jira.JIRA.createmeta_issuetypes(<KEY>)` +
  `createmeta_fieldtypes(<KEY>, <id>)` (public createmeta API); stub only for a
  `required: true` field NOT in the create BASELINE (see AC footer).
- transition hints (best-effort) → grounded in the ACTUAL transitions surface:
  `jira.JIRA.search_issues(jql)` (CONFIRMED in DC adapter) fetches one sample issue per
  discovered type, then `jira.JIRA.transitions(issue)` (CONFIRMED at
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/transitions.py:80`). Jira returns transitions only from each
  sample's CURRENT status, so the set is inherently partial → flagged best-effort.
  `status_map` stays identity-seeded; transition data is an ADVISORY marker, not complete.

Anchor: `search_issues`, `transitions`, `fields` are confirmed in-repo on this same
`jira.JIRA` client (DC adapter); the vocabulary getters are documented pycontribs 3.x
public API.

Emit: build `{"projects": {<KEY>: {<layer>}}}`.
- Default (no `--write`): serialize that block to stdout as TOML. NEVER writes; reads only.
- `--write`: mirror `write_jira_config`'s target-selection + read-whole/mutate/atomic-
  replace. Target via `config._discover_project_config` → existing `rebar.toml`, else
  create `<repo_root>/rebar.toml`; user `pyproject.toml` is NEVER edited. Read with
  `tomllib`, DEEP-MERGE under `data["mapping"]["projects"][<KEY>]` (EXISTING keys win,
  hand edits never clobbered), re-emit the WHOLE file via the orchestrator below, atomic
  `os.replace`.

Serialization — OPTION B, a top-level ORCHESTRATOR (a real `rebar.toml` mixes FLAT
siblings `[jira]`/`[tracker]` with the NESTED `[mapping.*]`, so no single emitter can
write the whole file). `_config_writer._emit_toml` (:188) fail-closes on any nested
sub-table — pinned by `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py:149`
(`_emit_toml({"jira": {"nested": {"k": "v"}}})` must raise `ConfigError`); UNTOUCHED. S8
adds two NEW helpers in `_config_writer.py`:
- `_emit_nested_toml(name, table)` — recurses one nested table into dotted-header
  sub-tables (`[mapping.projects.KEY.status_map]`); only ever handed the `mapping` table.
- `_emit_config_toml(data)` — orchestrator: split off the reserved `mapping` key, emit
  ALL remaining top-level items (scalars + the flat `[jira]`/`[tracker]` siblings it did
  NOT author) via the EXISTING `_emit_toml`, then append
  `_emit_nested_toml("mapping", data["mapping"])` when present, joined by a blank line.
`_emit_toml` never receives the `mapping` table, so its fail-closed contract + pinned test
stand; flat siblings round-trip through the flat path, nested `[mapping.*]` through the
nested path. The `--write` handler calls `_emit_config_toml`; `write_jira_config` keeps
calling `_emit_toml` unchanged. HONEST SCOPE: `tomllib` drops comments (no tomlkit), so
the merge keeps existing hand-edited VALUES (existing keys win) but inline comments in
`[mapping]` are NOT preserved.

## Scope
- NEW `mapping_probe.py` (probe port + per-axis getters + layer builder + TOML emit),
  <800 LOC.
- NEW `_config_writer._emit_nested_toml` + `_emit_config_toml` orchestrator (per
  Serialization); `_emit_toml` (:188) + pinned `tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py:149`
  stay UNTOUCHED.
- Wire: `bridge.py` parser, `_bridge_commands.py` dispatch, `__init__.py` handler (NEW).
- Out of scope: WRITE to Jira; live-credential CI gating; comment round-tripping.

## Testing
Tests use a FAKE probe port returning canned issue-type/priority/link-type/status/
createmeta/search+transitions data — fully offline, no live Jira or CI credential
(portability rule). A live smoke run is manual, never a CI gate. New tests in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_probe.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `test_probe_emits_mapping` — `rebar bridge suggest-mapping <KEY>` against the fake
      port emits a `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block with discovered vocabulary (`issue_types`,
      `statuses`, `link_types`, priorities, `hierarchy` when `hierarchyLevel` present),
      identity-seed axis maps, and `create_defaults` stubs.
- [x] `test_probe_is_read_only` — default invocation writes NO file; the fake port
      records only reads (no create/transition/delete), distinct from `check-access`.
- [x] `test_probe_write_preserves_edits` — `--write` into a `rebar.toml` that already
      has flat `[jira]`+`[tracker]` sections PRESERVES both AND adds `[mapping.*]`;
      deep-merge under `projects.<KEY>` keeps a pre-existing hand-edited mapping key
      (existing keys win); `pyproject.toml` is never edited.
- [x] `test_probe_transitions_best_effort` — fake port returns `search_issues` samples +
      per-issue `transitions()` limited to each sample's current status; emitted
      transition hints are flagged best-effort/partial (comment/marker), never asserted
      complete; `status_map` stays identity-seeded.

"create_defaults" baseline (concrete): the outbound create path
`adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py:140-158` (`map_local_to_remote`) already supplies
`summary`, `description`, `issuetype`, `priority`, `assignee`, conditionally `status`+
`parent`; a stub is emitted ONLY for a createmeta `required: true` field NOT in that
baseline.

Test tier: unit
